habitat: Alluvial floodplains, roadsides, open parks and village homesteads
distribution: Widely cultivated across all districts of Bangladesh
silviculturalNotes: Large spreading canopy with umbrella-shaped crown. Leaves fold up during overcast rainy weather and at nightfall. Fast-growing and nitrogen-fixing.

habitat: Well-drained upland terraces, red alluvial hillocks, and village homesteads
distribution: Nationwide; extensive commercial agroforests in Sylhet, Gazipur, and Modhupur
silviculturalNotes: Evergreen tree producing massive cauliflorous fruit on main trunk. Timber is golden-yellow aging to dark mahogany, highly resistant to termites and fungal decay.

habitat: Moist semi-evergreen and evergreen mixed forests and homestead orchards
distribution: Sylhet, Chittagong, and central homesteads across Bangladesh
silviculturalNotes: Moderate-sized evergreen tree. Flowers in white fragrant racemes during April-May; drupes ripen during autumn and early winter.

habitat: Avenues, botanical gardens, and campus borders with moist fertile soils
distribution: Planted widely along highways, institutional campuses, and tea gardens in Sylhet
silviculturalNotes: Very tall graceful tree reaching 35-40m with a smooth whitish-grey straight bole and airy delicate bipinnate foliage.

habitat: Lowland plains, roadsides, rural haats, and heritage sites
distribution: Found in every union and village across Bangladesh
silviculturalNotes: Strangler fig developing massive pillar-like prop roots supporting a giant horizontal crown. Provides critical food for birds, bats, and arboreal mammals.

habitat: Moist alluvial lowlands, riverbanks, and wetland margins
distribution: Abundant throughout Bangladesh; iconic on SUST campus hillocks and lakes
silviculturalNotes: Rapidly growing pioneer tree. Produces distinctive spherical orange blossom globes during the monsoon. Syn: Anthocephalus indicus / Anthocephalus chinensis.

habitat: Riparian river corridors, streams, and damp alluvial ravines
distribution: Riparian tracts in Sylhet, Rajshahi, and central floodplains
silviculturalNotes: Large buttressed trunk with smooth pinkish-grey exfoliating bark. Fruits are 5-winged fibrous samaras dispersed by water currents.

habitat: Floodplains, swamps, haor margins, and wet low-lying tracts
distribution: Sylhet wetlands, Chittagong, Dhaka avenues, SUST campus
silviculturalNotes: Medium deciduous tree celebrated for vibrant lilac-purple blooms in May-June. Highly resistant to water immersion.

habitat: Urban avenues, institutional gardens, and campus borders
distribution: Universally planted along educational campuses and streets throughout Bangladesh
silviculturalNotes: Columnar evergreen tree with drooping wavy-margined leaves. Excellent windbreak and dust attenuator in university campuses.

habitat: Dry to sub-humid plains and village homesteads
distribution: Nationwide; exceptionally abundant in the northern Barind tract
silviculturalNotes: Hardy drought-tolerant evergreen tree. Enriches degraded soils, repels agricultural pests, and coppices freely.

habitat: Avenues, roadsides, and tea estate boundaries
distribution: Sylhet tea estates and institutional avenues
silviculturalNotes: Fast-growing high-canopy tree with bipinnate leaves. Highly valued for tea garden shade management and microclimate buffering.

habitat: Seasonally submerged freshwater haor swamps and riverbanks
distribution: Sylhet-Sunamganj Haor Basin (Tanguar Haor, Hakaluki Haor)
silviculturalNotes: Critical ecological species capable of withstanding complete root inundation for 5-6 months during monsoon floods.

habitat: Moist evergreen and semi-evergreen hill valleys
distribution: Hill forests of Sylhet, Chittagong, and homestead botanical gardens
silviculturalNotes: Graceful evergreen tree noted for intensely fragrant golden-yellow blossoms. Requires rich, porous, humic soils.

habitat: Dry to moist tropical plains, homesteads, and roadsides
distribution: Cultivated in villages and along highways nationwide
silviculturalNotes: Long-lived evergreen tree with dense drooping foliage. Highly resistant to strong cyclonic winds due to deep taproot.

habitat: Lowland rainforests and riparian fringes of evergreen hill forests
distribution: Sylhet (Lawachara, Rema-Kalenga) and Chittagong Hill Tracts
silviculturalNotes: Magnificent emergent tree with smooth cylindrical bole. Timber is exceptionally dense, durable, and naturally termite resistant.

habitat: Coastal sand dunes, riverbanks, campuses, and parks
distribution: Coastal belts, Cox's Bazar, and planted across all university campuses
silviculturalNotes: Characteristic horizontal whorled branching like a pagoda. Leaves turn vivid scarlet-red before shedding in winter.

habitat: Degraded red clay hills, roadside embankments, and social forestry strips
distribution: Extensively planted nationwide across all forest divisions
silviculturalNotes: Fast-growing exotic phyllodinous legume. Tolerates drought and low-nutrient acidic soils. Excellent coppicing ability.

habitat: Plantations, roadside avenues, homestead agroforests
distribution: Extensively cultivated across Bangladesh since colonial introduction
silviculturalNotes: Premium reddish-brown hardwood. Susceptible to Hypsipyla robusta shoot borer in early sapling stages.

habitat: Moist evergreen hill forests, stream banks, and haor swamp edges
distribution: Sylhet hill streams, Lawachara, Sundarbans fringe, and village ponds
silviculturalNotes: Spreading evergreen tree with corrugated leathery leaves and large white flowers. Hard woody fruits eaten by wild elephants.

habitat: Tropical wet evergreen and semi-evergreen hill forests
distribution: Sylhet (Lawachara, Rema-Kalenga), Chittagong, Cox's Bazar, CHT
silviculturalNotes: Giant emergent tree reaching 45-50m height. Produces iconic two-winged samaras dispersed by rotational spinning in May-June.

habitat: Moist evergreen and semi-evergreen hill rainforests
distribution: Sylhet hill tracts, Lawachara National Park, CHT
silviculturalNotes: Large evergreen tree with rough brown-grey bark. Seeds are recalcitrant and germinate rapidly in moist forest litter.

habitat: Subtropical acidic red hill slopes with high humidity
distribution: Sylhet Division (Barlekha, Kulaura, Sreemangal)
silviculturalNotes: Famous aromatic tree where dark heartwood resin forms in response to fungal infection. Artificial nailing technique widely researched at SUST FES.

habitat: Deciduous and semi-evergreen hill slopes, gardens, campuses
distribution: Sylhet, CHT, and cultivated nationwide
silviculturalNotes: Small to medium deciduous tree covered in fragrant pink-purple orchid-like blossoms in late winter. Twin-lobed bilobed leaves.

habitat: Deciduous forests, homestead boundaries, dry sandy tracts
distribution: Common in rural homesteads and dry forest fringes across Bangladesh
silviculturalNotes: Medium deciduous tree with smooth grey bark. Highly noted for vegetative propagation; cuttings root easily to establish living boundary fences.

habitat: Moist deciduous and evergreen forest borders and campus grounds
distribution: Found across all divisions of Bangladesh
silviculturalNotes: Whorled tier branching with bitter white milky sap. Highly fragrant greenish-white flowers perfume autumn evenings in October.

habitat: Well-drained alluvial and sandy-loam hill slopes
distribution: Extensive forest plantations in Sylhet, Chittagong, and CHT
silviculturalNotes: Introduced to Bangladesh in 1871. Deciduous timber monarch; thick spongy endocarp seeds require weathering before nursery germination.

habitat: Tropical moist deciduous terraced tracts with red clay (Modhupur/Bhawal Garh)
distribution: Central Dhaka-Mymensingh-Tangail belt and northern Dinajpur
silviculturalNotes: Gregarious light-demander with extraordinary coppicing power. Thick fire-resistant bark protects stands during dry season surface fires.

habitat: Deciduous forest tracts, riverbanks, and open village countryside
distribution: Abundant throughout all rural regions of Bangladesh
silviculturalNotes: Massive buttressed trunk with conical prickles when young. Fiery red blossoms cover leafless branches in February-March.

habitat: Mixed dry deciduous hill forests and homestead orchards
distribution: Sylhet, Chittagong Hill Tracts, and village homesteads nationwide
silviculturalNotes: Small to medium deciduous tree with light feathery foliage. Fruits are round ribbed drupes celebrated in Ayurvedic medicine.

habitat: River valleys, swamp fringes, moist deciduous forests, and roadsides
distribution: Common nationwide in both forests and rural landscapes
silviculturalNotes: Tall pioneer tree with conspicuous smooth greenish-white bark peeling in thin papery flakes. Excellent nitrogen-fixer.

habitat: Dry to moist plains, village homesteads, and highway avenues
distribution: Found throughout Bangladesh; hardy in drought-prone areas
silviculturalNotes: Dark grey rough fissured bark with sweet-scented pompom flowers. Dry pods rattle conspicuously in winter breezes.

habitat: Deciduous plains, degraded soils, open grasslands and forest margins
distribution: Central and northern Bangladesh, campus grounds
silviculturalNotes: Medium deciduous tree with trifoliate leaves. Canopy erupts into dazzling vermilion-orange flowers in spring (February-March).

habitat: Tropical wet evergreen rainforests of Sylhet and CHT
distribution: Sylhet hill reserves (Lawachara, Rema-Kalenga) and Chittagong
silviculturalNotes: Slow-growing evergreen tree with exceptionally dense, heavy timber. Flush of young leaves is brilliant crimson-pink.

habitat: Deciduous forests, open woodlands, and campus avenues
distribution: Cultivated nationwide; famous on SUST academic avenue in summer
silviculturalNotes: Medium deciduous tree hanging with pendulous racemes of bright yellow flowers in April-May, followed by long cylindrical brown pods.

habitat: Subtropical evergreen hill peaks and high-ridge crests
distribution: High hills of Chittagong Hill Tracts and northeastern Sylhet ridges
silviculturalNotes: One of the very few indigenous gymnosperms of Bangladesh. Leaves resemble bamboo foliage (hence Banspata). Highly prized timber.

habitat: Alluvial river beds, highway strips, and farm boundaries
distribution: Widespread across northern and central Bangladesh
silviculturalNotes: Deciduous timber tree with golden-brown heartwood. Susceptible to vascular wilt fungus (Fusarium solani) in waterlogged soils.

habitat: Mixed deciduous and dry hill forests
distribution: Sylhet, Chittagong, and homestead herbal plantations
silviculturalNotes: Medium deciduous tree producing ribbed drupes rich in hydrolyzable tannins. Regarded as 'King of Medicines' in indigenous pharmacopeia.

habitat: Moist deciduous and semi-evergreen hill tracts
distribution: Sylhet, Modhupur tract, and Chittagong forests
silviculturalNotes: Massive deciduous tree with tall buttressed trunk and round velvety fruits. Honeybees favor its fragrant nectar.

habitat: Botanical arboreta, university campuses, and shrine groves
distribution: Planted in SUST botanical grounds, Mirpur National Botanical Garden, Baldha Garden
silviculturalNotes: Extraordinary tree bearing woody cannonball-sized fruits directly on tangled flowering racemes growing out of the trunk (cauliflory).

habitat: Evergreen and semi-evergreen rainforests and hill valleys
distribution: Sylhet hill tracts, Lawachara, Rema-Kalenga, and CHT
silviculturalNotes: Large evergreen canopy tree with smooth grey bark and thick leathery leaves. Fruits provide abundant sustenance for forest birds.

habitat: Intertidal mangrove mudflats and river banks in the Sundarbans
distribution: Sundarbans Mangrove Forest (Khulna, Bagerhat, Satkhira)
silviculturalNotes: Mangrove tree with thin buttresses resembling serpentine ribbons. Produces large spherical woody fruits that break into tetrahedral seeds.

habitat: Intertidal newly accreted coastal mudflats and estuarine chars
distribution: Coastal green belt afforestation across Noakhali, Bhola, Patuakhali, and Sundarbans
silviculturalNotes: Pioneer mangrove species with tall pointed pneumatophores (respiratory roots) that rapidly trap silt to stabilize coastal land.

habitat: Slightly elevated mangrove ridges and riverbanks in the Sundarbans
distribution: Sundarbans Mangrove Biosphere Reserve
silviculturalNotes: Produces beautiful dark reddish-brown heartwood. Possesses blunt pneumatophores and dark fissured bark.

habitat: Pioneering intertidal banks and high-salinity zones
distribution: Sundarbans and all coastal mangrove delta networks
silviculturalNotes: Characterized by dense carpets of pencil-like pencil pneumatophores projecting vertically from lateral roots to breathe during tidal immersion.

habitat: Moderately saline mangrove areas in the Sundarbans
distribution: Sundarbans Mangrove Reserve
silviculturalNotes: Dominant species in central Sundarbans. Contains blistering white latex capable of causing temporary blindness if contact occurs with eyes.

habitat: Dense interior tidal thickets and saline mangrove banks
distribution: Southern saline tracts of the Sundarbans
silviculturalNotes: Shrub or small mangrove tree forming impenetrable thickets. Remarkable for viviparous germination where seedlings germinate while still attached to parent tree.

habitat: Soft muddy banks and brackish water river margins
distribution: Sundarbans river networks and estuarine coastal channels
silviculturalNotes: Trunkless mangrove palm with creeping horizontal rhizomes. Huge pinnate fronds up to 9m long are the primary sustainable non-timber forest product of Sundarbans.

habitat: Interior high-saline estuarine zones of the Sundarbans
distribution: Sundarbans Mangrove Reserve
silviculturalNotes: Large mangrove tree with knee-roots (pneumatophores bending like bent knees) and prominent scarlet-red calyx lobes. Viviparous seedlings.

habitat: Canal banks and river edges with frequent tidal washing
distribution: Throughout Sundarbans mangrove waterways
silviculturalNotes: Small tree with fragrant white blooms that yield the most sought-after white honey collected by the traditional Mouvals of the Sundarbans.

habitat: Freshwater and low-salinity zones of the Sundarbans
distribution: Northeastern and eastern sectors of the Sundarbans Mangrove Biosphere
silviculturalNotes: The namesake keystone tree of the Sundarbans. Dense peg-like pneumatophores. Affected by 'top dying' physiological disorder caused by rising salinity.

habitat: Tropical wet evergreen hill forests and deep moist ravines
distribution: Chittagong Hill Tracts, Cox's Bazar, and Sylhet hill valleys
silviculturalNotes: Towering emergent tree with immense plank buttresses reaching over 40-50m height. Disperses through 5-winged samara-like fruit.

habitat: Subtropical moist hill valleys and streamsides
distribution: Sylhet hill ranges, CHT, and tea estate ravines
silviculturalNotes: Deciduous tree with reddish fragrant wood resembling true mahogany. Wind-dispersed winged seeds ripen in May-June.

habitat: Moist deciduous and semi-evergreen hill slopes
distribution: Sylhet, Chittagong, and major forest plantations across Bangladesh
silviculturalNotes: Fast-growing light-demanding pioneer tree. Highly vigorous coppicer; vulnerable to Calopepla leayana defoliator beetle in monotypic stands.

uses: Longest / Tallest Tree of Bangladesh Forest
habitat: Primary virgin evergreen rainforests in deep hill valleys
distribution: Chittagong Hill Tracts (Kassalong, Rainkheong) and Cox's Bazar
silviculturalNotes: Celebrated as the tallest emergent tree species recorded in Bangladesh natural forests, towering up to 60 meters with a massive cylindrical clear bole.

habitat: Moist forest borders, roadsides, and university campus grounds
distribution: Found in all forest divisions and campus arboreta across Bangladesh
silviculturalNotes: Iconic tier-branched tree known for its intensely sweet autumn night fragrance and whorled glabrous leaves. Milky latex in all tissues.
